entry.title: I Survived 100 Days On The Zombie Titanic. The Final Day Changes Everything. (Full Movie)

media:group.media:title: I Survived 100 Days On The Zombie Titanic. The Final Day Changes Everything. (Full Movie)
media:group.media:description:
Stickman survival: a zombie survival story, day by day. The Titanic hits the iceberg, the dead wake up below deck, and this time she doesn't sink. You have to survive 100 days on her in the ice. The full movie: Day 1 to Day 100 in one video.
A scream comes down the escape ladder in Boiler Room 5. The watertight doors slam shut. You climb, and you learn the rules that keep you alive: shut every door behind you, and sound carries in steel.
Day 1 to Day 100: a raid down the Grand Staircase. A message every night at 2:17 a.m.: "We see your lights." A sealer frozen in the ice twelve miles north. Scotland Road full of the dead, and a captain who never left his cabin.
Real Titanic facts all the way through: coal and boilers, watertight compartments, lifeboats, Morse code and pack ice.

entry.title: Blizzard Survival: 30 Days Locked Inside a Cabin

media:group.media:title: Blizzard Survival: 30 Days Locked Inside a Cabin
media:group.media:description:
It is 4:40 in the afternoon. You deliver firewood for a living, this is your last stop, and the road behind you is about to disappear.
You are 14 miles above town in somebody else's cabin. Wood is not the problem. The problem is one stove for a whole cabin, pipes that freeze on the second morning, a truck you must not run, a radio that says this is not a storm that will pass, and a note from the owner asking you to do one thing: please don't move the thermometer.
Chapters 0:00 Snow Falls Toward What Is Warm 1:45 Problem 1: The Heat 3:18 Problem 2: The Water 4:25 Day 3: Stay Dry 5:23 Day 7: The Routine 6:12 Day 9: Whiteout 6:35 Day 12: A Voice Outside 7:22 Problem 3: The Chimney 8:42 Problem 4: The Living 9:10 Day 22: Something Is Heating It 9:34 Day 25: The Last Broadcast 10:13 Day 30
Real facts in this story: - Eating snow burns body heat. Melt it first. - About 10 inches of snow melts into roughly 1 inch of water. - Leaving a tap dripping helps stop pipes from freezing, because moving water freezes more slowly. - A buried tailpipe can push car exhaust inside. Carbon monoxide has no colour and no smell. - Wet clothes pull heat out of your body many times faster than dry air. - Early hypothermia: stumbles, mumbles, fumbles and grumbles. You are usually the last to notice. - Frostnip: warm skin slowly. Don't rub it and don't hold it against a stove. - A cold chimney can push smoke into the room instead of drawing it out. - Creosote builds up inside chimneys and can start chimney fires.
This is a fictional animated story. The survival facts are general knowledge, not medical or safety advice. In a real emergency, follow your local authorities.
What would you have done on Day 30? Tell me in the comments. Subscribe for Part 2: Day 31 to Day 60.
